findings.title: Container restart policy is set to 'no'
likely_causes: Container launched without --restart unless-stopped or on-failure
findings.recommendation: Use `--restart on-failure:5` or `unless-stopped` for long-running services.

findings.title: Single-stage build using full SDK/OS base image `python:3.11` ships compilers and build toolchains to production

evidence.recommended_runtime_base: python:3.11-slim-bookworm (scratch is unsuitable for CPython interpreter and manylinux C extensions)

likely_causes: No multi-stage separation between build environment and runtime image
findings.recommendation: Use a multi-stage build and copy only runtime artifacts into `python:3.11-slim-bookworm (scratch is unsuitable for CPython interpreter and manylinux C extensions)`.

findings.title: apt-get install without cleaning `/var/lib/apt/lists/*` in the same RUN instruction

evidence.run_instruction: RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential git

likely_causes: Apt package lists remain permanently committed in the lower overlayfs layer
findings.recommendation: Chain `&& rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*` inside the exact same `RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ...` command.

findings.title: pip install executed without `--no-cache-dir` or BuildKit cache mount
likely_causes: pip stores downloaded wheel archives in ~/.cache/pip inside the image layer
findings.recommendation: Pass `pip install --no-cache-dir` or set `ENV PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1`.

findings.title: `COPY . .` appears before dependency installation, invalidating dependency layer cache on every code edit
likely_causes: Copying full source tree before lockfiles/manifests
findings.recommendation: Copy only `package*.json` / `requirements.txt` / `go.mod` / `Cargo.toml` first, install dependencies, and then `COPY . .`.

findings.title: `.dockerignore` is missing critical exclusions: .git, .env, node_modules, __pycache__, .venv
likely_causes: Incomplete .dockerignore risks leaking .env secrets or .git history into COPY . . layers
findings.recommendation: Add `.git`, `.env*`, `node_modules`, `.venv`, `__pycache__`, and `target/` to `.dockerignore`.

findings.title: Dockerfile does not switch to a non-root USER in the final stage
likely_causes: Container processes run as UID 0 by default unless USER is specified
findings.recommendation: Create an unprivileged user (`RUN useradd -u 10001 -r -s /sbin/nologin appuser`) and set `USER 10001`.

findings.title: Large image layer #1 (965.12 MiB)
likely_causes: Compiler toolchain, unstripped binaries, or uncleaned package cache committed to layer
findings.recommendation: Move build tools to a builder stage in a multi-stage Dockerfile and copy only runtime artifacts.

findings.title: Large image layer #2 (233.65 MiB)

evidence.created_by: /bin/sh -c apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential git

likely_causes: Compiler toolchain, unstripped binaries, or uncleaned package cache committed to layer
findings.recommendation: Move build tools to a builder stage in a multi-stage Dockerfile and copy only runtime artifacts.

findings.title: Cleanup command executed in a separate `RUN` layer does not reclaim bytes from parent layers
likely_causes: OverlayFS layers are immutable; deleting files in a later layer only writes whiteout markers
findings.recommendation: Combine package installation and cache cleanup (`&& rm -rf ...`) into a single `RUN` layer.

findings.title: Large image layer #4 (171.66 MiB)
likely_causes: Compiler toolchain, unstripped binaries, or uncleaned package cache committed to layer
findings.recommendation: Move build tools to a builder stage in a multi-stage Dockerfile and copy only runtime artifacts.

findings.title: Container runs as root (UID 0)
likely_causes: No non-root USER specified in Dockerfile or container securityContext
findings.recommendation: Run container as a non-root UID (e.g., `--user 10001:10001`).

findings.title: Container is running in `--privileged` mode (disables seccomp, AppArmor, and device isolation)
likely_causes: Container launched with --privileged flag
findings.recommendation: Remove `--privileged` and grant only minimal required Linux capabilities.

findings.title: Excessive Linux capabilities granted: CAP_SYS_ADMIN, NET_ADMIN
likely_causes: Overly permissive CapAdd configuration
findings.recommendation: Drop all capabilities (`--cap-drop=ALL`) and add back only strictly necessary capabilities.

findings.title: Sensitive host path mounted into container: `/var/run/docker.sock` -> `/var/run/docker.sock`
likely_causes: Mounting Docker socket or sensitive host root directories allows trivial host root escape
findings.recommendation: Remove host `/var/run/docker.sock` or `/etc` mounts, or proxy read-only API calls via a hardened socket proxy.

findings.title: Container root filesystem is writable (`ReadonlyRootfs: false`)
likely_causes: Default Docker rootfs allows runtime binary tampering
findings.recommendation: Enable `--read-only` root filesystem and mount `/tmp` via `--tmpfs /tmp:rw,noexec,nosuid`.

findings.title: Missing `no-new-privileges:true` in SecurityOpt
likely_causes: Setuid/setgid binaries inside container can escalate privileges without no-new-privileges
findings.recommendation: Pass `--security-opt=no-new-privileges:true`.

findings.title: Missing cgroup memory or PIDs limit (`Memory=0` or `PidsLimit=unlimited`)
likely_causes: Container can exhaust host RAM or fork-bomb the node
findings.recommendation: Set explicit `--memory` and `--pids-limit` bounds on every container.

findings.title: Container is attached only to the default `bridge` network, where Docker embedded DNS (`127.0.0.11`) service discovery is disabled
likely_causes: Containers on the default docker0 bridge cannot resolve peer containers by container name
findings.recommendation: Create and attach a user-defined bridge network (`docker network create app-net`) to enable automatic DNS name resolution via 127.0.0.11.

findings.title: Exposed container port(s) `9090/tcp` have no host port publishing (`-p`)
likely_causes: EXPOSE in Dockerfile only documents the port; it does not publish the port to the host without -p / ports: in Compose
findings.recommendation: Publish the port explicitly (e.g., `-p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080`) or route via an internal reverse proxy on the same bridge network.

findings.title: Application command binds to `127.0.0.1`/`localhost` inside container, breaking Docker NAT port forwarding
likely_causes: Traffic forwarded via Docker bridge veth pair arrives on eth0, not container lo (127.0.0.1)
findings.recommendation: Bind the application server inside the container to `0.0.0.0` (e.g., `--host 0.0.0.0`).

findings.title: Confirmed kernel cgroup OOM kill (`State.OOMKilled=true`, `ExitCode=137`)
likely_causes: Container working set exceeded cgroup memory limit (`HostConfig.Memory`), triggering Linux kernel cgroup OOM killer
findings.recommendation: Increase container memory limit or configure runtime heap bounds (`GOMEMLIMIT`, `--max-old-space-size`, `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=80.0`) to 80-85% of the container limit.

findings.title: Container is in a restart loop (`RestartCount=7`)
likely_causes: Repeated process crash or failing healthcheck causing container supervisor to restart the container
findings.recommendation: Inspect logs from the previous run and fix the root cause reflected by `ExitCode` before increasing restart retries.

findings.title: Container healthcheck is UNHEALTHY (failing streak=5)

evidence.last_output: HTTP probe failed to connect to localhost port 8080: Connection refused

likely_causes: Healthcheck probe binary missing inside minimal container image, wrong port/loopback binding, or deadlocked application thread pool
findings.recommendation: Verify the healthcheck binary exists inside the container image and that `--start-period` is long enough for initialization.

findings.title: Kubernetes waiting condition `CrashLoopBackOff` on container `payment-processor` (kubelet backoff state; underlying container last terminated with exitCode=137, reason=OOMKilled)
likely_causes: CrashLoopBackOff is a Kubernetes kubelet backoff condition triggered because the container repeatedly exited (last exitCode=137, reason=OOMKilled)
findings.recommendation: Inspect previous pod logs (`kubectl logs <pod> --previous`) and remediate the underlying termination cause (`lastState.terminated`).
